chunks: Hadith 5564: Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb al-Kulaynī, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated from Ḥumayd ibn Ziyād, from Ibn Samāʿah, from Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him: A man from your followers died and left behind young children, and he left some property, but he also owed a debt of which the creditors are unaware. If it is paid to his creditors, his children will remain with nothing. So he said: Spend it on his children.

key_terms.أَنْفِقْهُ: spend it; use the property for maintenance
key_terms.الْغُرَمَاءُ: the creditors to whom the debt is owed
key_terms.دَيْنٌ: a financial debt owed by the deceased

ai.seo_question: What should be done with a deceased person's wealth if he owed an unknown debt and left behind young children?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the case of a deceased believer who leaves behind young children, some wealth, and an unpaid debt unknown to the creditors. The Imam عليه السلام instructs that the available wealth be spent on the children, highlighting a ruling connected to the protection of vulnerable dependents in this circumstance.
